title: Light: Shadows and Reflections
seo_title: Light Class 7 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Curiosity Chapter 11)
standard_text: Luminous and non-luminous objects; light travels in straight lines; transparent, translucent and opaque materials; shadows; the pinhole camera; reflection from plane mirrors, the laws of reflection and lateral inversion; periscope and kaleidoscope; curved mirrors in daily life (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 11).

key_sub: Angle of incidence = angle of reflection.
body_html:
How to think about it

Luminous objects such as the Sun and a candle flame give their own light; we see other objects because they reflect light into our eyes. Light travels in straight lines, so an opaque object blocks it and casts a dark shadow. A pinhole camera forms an upside-down image.

A plane mirror reflects light so that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection (both measured from the normal). Its image is upright, the same size, as far behind the mirror as the object is in front, and laterally inverted. Two mirrors at 45° make a periscope; the back of a spoon acts as a convex mirror.

Example

Light hits a mirror at 35° to the normal. Angle of reflection?

equal to the angle of incidence

Answer: 35°

Example

Stand 2 m from a mirror. Distance to your image?

image is 2 m behind

Answer: 4 m

Common mistakes

  • Measuring angles from the mirror instead of the normal.
  • Thinking a coloured object has a coloured shadow.
  • Saying the image in a pinhole camera is upright.

faq.q: Why does a pinhole camera give an upside-down image?
faq.a: Light travels in straight lines, so rays from the top of the object pass through the hole to the bottom of the screen, and the other way round.

items.e: The ground or a wall can act as a screen.
